decision: devlab kernel install refuses a kernel that is not an EFI executable.
why: The bootloader starts EFI programs only; a gzip kernel was lost before it could log a line.

decision: devlab health waits until the phone has been up 90 seconds before checking, saying so once.
why: Every job slept before a health check by hand (7 times); a check read too early fails for the wrong reason.
rejected: A fixed sleep in every script; checking at once and retrying failures.

decision: A listening test runs only with --placed, the word that the microphone is by the phone.
why: The first results came from a microphone being worn.
rejected: Un-naming the microphone's file as the safeguard: a trick only its author remembers.

decision: devlab kernel try waits for a new boot id and reports the outcome itself, judged from the running release, the entry's counter and the timeout log.
why: Booting a test kernel and reading what happened was the heaviest manual work (9 times, 54 effort-minutes), and guessing at it cost three reboots.
rejected: Waiting for the phone to go down and then up (it misfired twice: the try schedules its reboot); leaving the reading to a person.

decision: A change devlab makes to the phone ends with its health: after a reboot (phone reboot, kernel try) devlab waits for the report that boot writes by itself, rather than running the suite again; after a change without a reboot (provision) it runs the suite now. Either way the report is brought to the lab and an unhealthy phone fails the command.
why: Nobody has to remember to check; and waiting for the boot's own report measures exactly what every boot of the phone measures - the lab adds no second way of checking.
rejected: Running the suite from the lab after each reboot (two runs per boot, and the lab's run would be the one that differs from an unattended boot); leaving the health check as a separate step to remember.

decision: devlab files the phone's reports into the picture through tad (one tad sql statement per run: its rows read from the report, its counts from those rows; tad keeps it only if every rule holds, then canonical form and the rendered pages), and devlab watch, after every boot, waits for the phone's own report, says its verdict on the board, and gathers with --land: in devlab's own clones of the lab and the picture, each landed through land, signed devlab. The face is drawn again by the picture's CI on that landing.
why: The author, 2026-11-17: tad is the open database shared by the whole linux-phone project; devlab reports the suites' results into it by itself and the pages reflect them - not an agent doing it by hand each time. devlab's own clones keep its landings out of the clones people and agents work in (two hands in one clone once merged each other's changes).
rejected: devlab appending JSON lines itself (rows tad never checked); the watch running the lab-side checks over SSH (a second way of measuring beside the phone's own); landing from ~/Projects (collides with work in progress there).

decision: devlab gather now brings every report the phone keeps that the lab lacks into the device lab's tests/results (RUN.jsonl, as written on the phone), and files every run not yet filed into linux-phone-oco/docs' test_results and test_runs, the rows made from the report's lines. A run is filed once, by its id.
why: Filing was by hand (tests/to-docs.sh, through tad's Python) and had fallen a week behind: docs held 7 runs from 2026-11-10 while the lab had made many since. Rust carries it now, and the tables stay where they are declared and observed today.
rejected: Declaring test_runs and test_results again in each device lab (one nature, two declarations - entered as the sign a-test-run-has-no-shared-shape in ocoeco, to be answered in the language); keeping to-docs.sh (new filing through Python).

decision: The phone measures its own health after every boot: devlab-health, a static Rust runner, runs small check files (base layer, then shell layer) and writes one report per run in test_results' shape, keeping the evidence when unhealthy. The checks are POSIX shell in postmarketOS's test shape and print plain words (pass|fail|skip TEST COMPONENT detail); the runner makes the JSON, the verdict and the evidence. Generic checks live in lab-tools; what a phone is expected to have is its manifest's [health], and a phone's own checks sit beside the generic ones.
why: Health measured only from the lab is health only while the lab is connected and remembers to ask; a phone that checks itself after every boot leaves a record for every change. Shipped code is Rust (2026-11-11-rust-for-what-ships): strings and structure - JSON escaping, the report - are where shell is fragile. The probes themselves only read sysfs and the system's own tools, which is what postmarketOS's tests and bootrr do in shell, so they can be contributed there.
rejected: A shell runner (JSON escaping and report shaping in sh - the fragility the Rust decision answers); checks written in Rust (a probe of sysfs gains nothing, and upstream would not take it); keeping the checks run only from the lab over SSH (no record when the lab is not asking); one check file per device (surya's checks.sh: nothing reusable for the next phone).

decision: The health suite reaches phones as an Alpine package (devlab-health: the runner, the checks, the unit and the timer) published through the package conveyor once it publishes Alpine repositories (cv-apk); until then devlab puts the same files on the phone itself, as the development path.
why: The commons has one packaging conveyor that every project calls (linux-package-distribution-oco/conveyor) and it already builds aarch64-musl binaries; a package is how postmarketOS installs and updates anything, and it gives the phone updates the way the lab machine already gets them.
rejected: devlab copying files onto the phone for good (a second delivery route beside the conveyor; nothing updates it); building the package in lab-tools' own CI (copying what the conveyor exists to do once).

decision: devlab offers its structured door over MCP (devlab mcp, stdio, with rmcp): run, put and get a file, the health report, kernel install, try and status, reboot and wait - each the same function the command line calls.
why: Agent access plans every tool's structured door over MCP in Rust with rmcp, devlab among the first (aa-two-doors); an agent then works with the phone without a person and without a shell's quoting layer.
rejected: A separate MCP server project beside devlab (two doors to keep in step); MCP through a generic shell tool (every call a quoting puzzle).
